You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

memory_text = '''ARC task-f0196f49 TEST-VERIFIED rule (solved after 5 wrong submissions, 8 demos): Erase every color-5 object cell and replace it by one solid color-5 centerline. Preserve/recenter the black 0 frame around that centerline. Determine orientation from the black frame, not merely the object's bounding box: (1) If the input has one central vertical 0 line and two outer horizontal 0 lines, output a HORIZONTAL 5 line. Move the horizontal 0 lines to one row above and below the object's center row; retain the central vertical 0 line except where the 5 line crosses it. (2) If the input has TWO vertical 0 lines on the sides and a horizontal 0 line through the object, output a VERTICAL 5 line. Delete the original side 0 lines and draw new vertical 0 lines one column left/right of the object's center column; retain the horizontal 0 line except where the 5 line crosses it. The 5 line length equals the number of original 5 cells for odd counts (usually; an even-count demo sometimes drew count+1). Center it on the object's bounding-box center/median, clipping at grid boundaries. The verified 17x17 test had 15 gray cells, bounding rows 5..11 and cols 5..11, side 0 lines at cols 4 and 12, and horizontal 0 line at row 8. Correct output: vertical 0 lines at cols 7 and 9 on every row; vertical 5 line at col 8 rows 1..15 inclusive; row 8 all 0 except col 8=5; all other cells 7; original 0 lines at cols 4 and 12 removed. REJECTED variants: horizontal 5 line at row 8 with 0 bars rows 7/9 (wrong orientation), whether line cols 5..11, 1..15, or 0..14; vertical line at col 7 with 0 bars cols 6/8 (wrong center). Correct center was bounding-box center col 8, not mean/center-of-mass col 7.'''
